items.title: Helen Oakley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: Duke would sit there on the piano and he’d just hammer away a minute or two and he’d look over and say, “Rab, come up with something.” Rabbitt.

ctx.x: What’s the number of records at that time which would have meant a good release?

Well you see there were two labels. Duke’s things were really the band, was on the Master label. So then they had to make the money. They had to do “Sophisticated Lady” and all the things that would make the money. And they did. And my things, I was much better off, because my label was the thirty-five cent label, and it was the jazz label, and of course I think really those small band records have proven themselves over the years. Because they are still thought wonderful by the musicians. Mostly all musicians…
Oh that’s a marvelous story. And when Ellington would just sit and play those chords, was that, do you think that was fairly spontaneous?
